title: The regulation triggers the five-day partial-fill limit off the prescriber's address
rule_summary: 105 CMR 721.055(A) states the Massachusetts patient-requested partial fill as a duty: a pharmacist filling a Prescription for a schedule II controlled substance SHALL, IF REQUESTED BY THE PATIENT, dispense the substance in a lesser quantity than indicated, pursuant to M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 18(d3/4). It then supplies the operative trigger for the five-day limit: IF THE PRESCRIPTION WAS ISSUED BY A PRESCRIBER FROM A LOCATION OTHER THAN THE COMMONWEALTH, AS INDICATED BY THE ADDRESS OF THE PRESCRIBER ON THE PRESCRIPTION, the Prescription MUST BE PRESENTED FOR INITIAL PARTIAL FILL NOT LATER THAN FIVE CALENDAR DAYS after the Prescription issue date. That is a different test from the statute's 'filled pursuant to subsection (d) or (d1/2)': the pharmacist reads the address on the face of the prescription rather than adjudicating which statutory subsection the prescription travelled under, and the count is expressly in CALENDAR days. Under 721.055(B) the remaining portion may be filled on patient request provided only the same pharmacy that dispensed the lesser quantity dispenses it and it is filled not later than 30 days after the issue date, and under 721.055(C) the pharmacist or designee makes a notation in the patient record, accessible to the prescribing practitioner on request, of the partial fill and the quantity dispensed.
exam_relevance: Tests the trigger a pharmacist actually applies at the counter. The five-day limit is easy to file under 'out-of-state pathways'; the regulation keys it to the prescriber address printed on the prescription and counts calendar days.

numeric_facts.fact: Initial partial fill where the prescriber address on the prescription is outside Massachusetts
numeric_facts.conditions: Measured from the prescription issue date; the prescription must be presented for initial partial fill within it

numeric_facts.fact: Remaining portion after a patient-requested partial fill
numeric_facts.conditions: From the prescription issue date, and only at the same pharmacy that dispensed the lesser quantity

exceptions: The five-calendar-day limit attaches only where the prescriber's address on the prescription is outside the Commonwealth.
common_confusions: Applying the five-day limit by asking which statutory subsection the prescription travelled under, when the regulation asks only what address appears on it.
Counting business days; 105 CMR 721.055(A) says calendar days.
Reading the lesser-quantity dispensing as discretionary, when both the statute and the regulation say the pharmacist shall dispense on patient request.
verification_notes: 105 CMR 721.055(A)-(C) read verbatim from the official publication on 2026-09-10. Added because the GPT-FRESH-B4-SG-REPAIR-V6A audit found SG-CII-LIFECYCLE stated the five-day limit only in the statute's subsection-based form, and no canonical rule carried the regulation.
